The solar furnace repair was the most significant corrective maintenance campaign in FY25. During this effort, NSTTF also addressed a key reliability contributor: spare part tracking and storage. A consolidated spare parts list was assembled during the repair process in direct response to this downtime and is expected to reduce the time to repair. Maximo’s spare part tracking will be used to manage this spare parts list in the FY26 to reduce downtime from supply chain challenges. 4.3. Maintenance Performance Tracking NSTTF continued using Maximo-enabled key performance indicators (KPIs) to quantify reliability and responsiveness and to support continuous improvement. FY25 KPI observations included mean time to repair (MTTR) and mean time between failures (MTBF). These KPI’s will be tuned in FY26 to better reflect test facility 15 constraints by excluding certain non-operational periods like non-sun hours. KPI’s tracked within Maximo are shown below in Figure 4. The MTBF was reduced to 524 days in FY25 from 600 days in FY24 and this can be attributed to the upgrades implemented to the heliostat field that required adjustments. In just one year, the MTTR was reduced from 1,400 hours in FY24 to just under 1,000 hours, a 29% reduction as averaged since the start of our historical data tracking in 2021. Figure 4. KPI’s a. MTBF and b. MTTR Targets are indicated by the light gray pointer and current values are indicated by the dark pointers.
